newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo '97 sugar output seen up to 260,000T - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo '97 sugar output seen up to 260,000T - agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia could produce up to 260,000 tonnes of white sugar despite a smaller sugar beet area, Tanjug news agency reported on Friday.

"Although the area under sugar beet is only 55,000 hectares, we could expect production of 250,000-260,000 tonnes of sugar this year," the report quoted Bogdan Beric, director of the Business Association for Industrial Crops, as saying.
"This will be enough to meet the already reduced domestic demand considering huge existing supplies of suggar on the local market," he said.
Yugoslav farmers failed to meet the government beet area target of 100,000 ha, set to utilise the capacity of the country's 15 refineries.
The beet area in 1996 was some 70,000 ha yielding 2.391 million tonnes of sugarbeet. The country produced some 270,000 tones of sugar.

Annual needs are estimated at around 300,000 tonnes, down some 100,000 tonnes against the country's consumption in the pre-war years. This is due to a drastic fall in the standard of living of the most of the 10.5 million population swollen with some 500,000 refugees.
Beric also said that sunflower area would be between 165,000-180,000 ha and soybean around 70,000 ha this year.
According to the government plan, 200,000 ha should have been sown with sunflower and 80,000 ha with soybean.
Experts blame unfavourable weather conditions and overdue payments for last year's crop for farmers' failure to meet sowing targets.
"Farmers still have not been paid some 100 million dinars ($17.8 million) for their 1996 industrial crops," Beric said. --Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
